subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: On a graph of product formed against time, a steeper line shows that the reaction is:
questions.explain: A steeper gradient means more product forms per second, so the reaction is faster.

questions.q: How many moles are in 100 g of calcium carbonate, CaCO3? (Mr = 100)
questions.explain: moles = mass/Mr = 100/100 = 1 mol.

questions.q: When magnesium burns, the mass appears to increase. Why?
options: The magnesium gives off a gas
Oxygen from the air combines with the magnesium
questions.explain: Oxygen from the air joins the magnesium to form magnesium oxide, so the solid mass increases.

questions.q: A reaction gives a theoretical yield of 200 g but produces 150 g. What is the percentage yield?
questions.explain: percentage yield = (150/200)x100 = 75%.

questions.q: A reaction reaches equilibrium only in a:
questions.explain: Equilibrium can only be reached in a closed system where nothing can enter or escape.

questions.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: It provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
It increases the concentration of reactants
questions.explain: Catalysts provide an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

questions.q: Which method could be used to measure the rate of a reaction that produces a gas?
options: Measuring the volume of gas collected over time
Measuring the colour of the flask
questions.explain: Collecting and measuring the volume of gas produced over time gives the rate.

questions.q: A solution has a concentration of 25 g/dm3. What mass of solute is in 2 dm3?
questions.explain: mass = concentration x volume = 25 x 2 = 50 g.

questions.q: In a closed system, the total mass of the products of a reaction is:
questions.explain: Mass is conserved, so the products have the same total mass as the reactants.

questions.q: According to collision theory, for a reaction to occur particles must collide and have at least what?
questions.explain: Particles must collide with energy equal to or greater than the activation energy to react.

questions.q: At a higher temperature, a greater proportion of colliding particles:
options: Have at least the activation energy
Have less than the activation energy
questions.explain: Heating gives more particles energy equal to or above the activation energy, so more collisions succeed.

questions.q: What is the concentration in mol/dm³ of a solution with 0.5 mol of solute in 2 dm³?
questions.explain: concentration = moles/volume = 0.5/2 = 0.25 mol/dm³.

questions.q: How does increasing temperature increase the rate of reaction?
options: Particles move faster and collide more often with more energy
questions.explain: Higher temperature gives particles more energy, so they collide more frequently and more energetically.

questions.q: Increasing the pressure of reacting gases increases the rate because:
options: The particles are closer together so collide more frequently
questions.explain: Higher pressure squeezes gas particles closer, increasing collision frequency.

questions.q: A solution contains 20 g of solute in 0.5 dm³. What is its concentration in g/dm³?
questions.explain: concentration = mass/volume = 20/0.5 = 40 g/dm³.

questions.q: What is the formula of the ionic compound aluminium oxide, from Al³⁺ and O²⁻?
questions.explain: Balancing charges (2×Al³⁺ = +6, 3×O²⁻ = −6) gives Al2O3.

questions.q: What happens to a catalyst during a reaction?
options: It is chemically unchanged at the end
It becomes part of the product
questions.explain: A catalyst is not used up and remains chemically unchanged after the reaction.

questions.q: Decreasing the concentration of a product in a system at equilibrium causes the equilibrium to shift towards the:
questions.explain: Removing product makes the equilibrium shift towards the products to replace what was lost.

questions.q: Lowering the temperature of a reaction decreases the rate because particles:
options: Collide less often and with less energy
questions.explain: Cooler particles move more slowly, so they collide less frequently and with less energy.

questions.q: A compound contains 0.2 mol carbon and 0.4 mol hydrogen. What is its empirical formula?
questions.explain: The ratio 0.2:0.4 simplifies to 1:2, giving CH2.

questions.q: What is the Mr of sodium hydroxide, NaOH? (Ar: Na=23, O=16, H=1)
For an exothermic forward reaction at equilibrium, increasing the temperature will:
options: Shift the equilibrium towards the reactants
Shift the equilibrium towards the products
questions.explain: Le Chatelier: raising temperature favours the endothermic direction, here the reverse (reactant) side.
